definitions.explanation: the state of being lazy or unwilling to work or make effort

examples.japanese: {怠惰|たいだ}な{生活|せいかつ}を{送|おく}る。
{怠惰|たいだ}は{成功|せいこう}の{敵|てき}だ。
examples.english: Laziness is the enemy of success.

examples.japanese: {怠惰|たいだ}な{自分|じぶん}を{変|か}えたいと{思|おも}っている。
examples.english: I want to change my lazy self.

notes:
USAGE:
- {怠惰|たいだ}な{生活|せいかつ} (idle life)
- {怠惰|たいだ}な{人|ひと} (lazy person)
- {怠惰|たいだ}に{過|す}ごす (to spend time idly)

NUANCE:
A formal, somewhat literary word. Carries moral judgment - implies laziness as a character flaw or vice.

RELIGIOUS CONTEXT:
One of the Seven Deadly Sins in Christian tradition (sloth).

RELATED:
- {怠|なま}ける (to be lazy - verb, more casual)
- {怠|おこた}る (to neglect - verb)
- {無精|ぶしょう} (laziness - more colloquial)
- {勤勉|きんべん} (diligence - antonym)
